what:
Addendum 2 item 3(a): the t = 0 cross-energy surplus of snapshot starts (engine 8.527 against the family
quadrature 7.757 at r = 20; 2.228 against 1.533 at r = 24).

1. Angular average of the settled primary source (reference state, phase 0): phi_s(r), pi_s(r) in shells.
2. Tail: fit A_s e^{-kappa_s r}/r on r = 12 to 18 (kappa_s from the source's settled omega); residual
   phi_s - tail for r = 12 to 26 (the non-evanescent part).
3. Cross energy of two copies at phases (0, 0), windowed (26, 30) as the snapshot start, by axisymmetric
   quadrature of the radial profiles (static.moments): (i) the measured profile (phi_s, pi_s); (ii) the measured
   core with the fitted evanescent tail beyond r = 12 and pi = 0 beyond 12; (iii) the family profile at the settled
   omega. (i) - (ii) is the part carried by the non-evanescent field; (ii) - (iii) the core difference.
4. What the residual does to V_N: its cross with the partner's core oscillates at (n - 1) omega and averages out of
   whole-period N, but stays in the conserved E at its t = 0 value.
Usage: PYTHONPATH=. python outputs/session4/testA/diag_surplus.py   (one process)

diagnosis.residual: non-evanescent field in the settled source beyond the tail: wavenumber 2.53-2.54 = k3 (the steady 3 omega radiation), rms 5.5e-4 in phi (7.5e-5 Phi0) and 1.4e-3 in phi_t over r = 12 to 30; larger than the evanescent tail beyond r ~ 19
diagnosis.surplus: axisymmetric quadrature of the measured angular-average profile reproduces the engine t = 0 cross energy (8.530 vs 8.527 at r = 20; 2.228 vs 2.2277 at r = 24). Replacing the tail beyond r = 12 by the fitted evanescent tail removes 0.94, 0.71, 0.70, 0.40 at r = 16, 20, 24, 28 and leaves 7.823 and 1.531 against the family 7.757 and 1.533 at r = 20 and 24. The surplus is the cross of each copy's windowed 3 omega cloud (out to the 26-30 window) with the partner's core: nearly r-independent while the partner core is inside the cloud, falling once it reaches the window taper.
diagnosis.effect_on_V_N: E + absorbed and E_box keep the t = 0 value of this cross term; whole-period N removes its 3 omega x omega cross. In the two r = 20 runs V_N sits +0.07 (in phase) and +0.09 (anti phase) above U_static, not +0.7, so most of it is compensated. The rest (~0.08, of unknown r dependence) is an offset comparable to U at r ~ 22 to 24: V_N cannot resolve U beyond about r = 24 without a control that removes it (e.g. singles and pairs from a source whose cloud is cut at a smaller window, or a pair-minus-superposed-copies run).
diagnosis.effect_on_V_F: the t = 0 cloud is outgoing at group velocity 0.93 and crosses the partner before t1 = 40 at r <= 30; its impulse is a constant velocity, taken by the c1 term of the fit. It does not enter the acceleration in the window. The steady 3 omega emission of each lump continues in every run (it is physics, not a start artefact): its cross force is the radiation-mediated term A3 lists (order 1e-4, sign alternating with k3 r), which V_F would see as a residual at large r.
